panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph showing thick skin with dark polygonal scales, a characteristic manifestation of X-linked recessive ichthyosis, directly supported by the caption and in-text attribution to family F2 patients. B: Clinical photograph of lower limbs showing polygonal, adherent, large dark scales characteristic of X-linked recessive ichthyosis, directly supported by caption and in-text. C: Clinical photograph showing scaling prominent on upper and lower limbs, thighs, and trunk, characteristic of X-linked recessive ichthyosis, directly supported by caption and in-text.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Clinical photograph of abdomen showing thick dark-brown polygonal scales, the hallmark cutaneous presentation of X-linked recessive ichthyosis (XLI/STS deficiency), in a patient from the reported family. [raw subtype: XLI (STS deficiency)] B: Clinical photograph of the back showing confluent dark-brown polygonal ichthyotic scales, consistent with the classic trunk involvement described for XLI in the caption and in-text. [raw subtype: XLI (STS deficiency)] C: Clinical photograph of the neck showing ichthyotic scaling, matching the caption's description of neck involvement in XLI patients. [raw subtype: XLI (STS deficiency)] D: Clinical photograph of the anterior trunk showing widespread dark-brown polygonal scales, a textbook manifestation of XLI as described in the caption. in_text_mentions: In all the patients from the family, the most prominent features included generalized dryness and dark brown scales prominent on the skin (Fig. 2); in which trunk, ears, scalp and limbs were affected. In almost all patients the abdomen was more severely affected than the back and other parts of the body. Scales were confluent and lighter on the scalp. Face, palms and soles were not involved. The hair and nails were normal. Preauricular small scales were also observed in young individuals.
